title: G-rings ascend along weakly etale Noetherian ring maps
statement: Let $A$ and $B$ be commutative Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $f:A\to B$ be weakly etale [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. If $A$ is a G-ring [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], then $B$ is a G-ring.

source.document: Silvio Greco, Two theorems on excellent rings, Nagoya Mathematical Journal 60 (1976), 139–149, DOI 10.1017/S0027763000017190
source.place: Theorem 5.3(i), with P = geometrically regular in Section 1.1; Remark 5.2 identifies the AF hypothesis with weak etaleness for Noetherian rings. Printed pp. 139–140, 146–147 (PDF pp. 1–2, 8–9). G-ring terminology: Stacks Tag 07GH (definition-G-ring).

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary prime $\mathfrak q\subset B$, put $\mathfrak p=f^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$, $R=A_{\mathfrak p}$ and $S=B_{\mathfrak q}$, and let $g:R\to S$ be the induced map. Weak etaleness supplies flatness of $f$ by [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-ring-maps], $R$ and $S$ are Noetherian local rings and $g$ is flat and local. Write $u:R\to\widehat R$ and $v:S\to\widehat S$ for their completion maps. The G-ring hypothesis on $A$, unfolded by [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], says exactly that $u$ is regular. It remains to show that $v$ is regular for every such $\mathfrak q$. If $B$ has no primes, this universal condition is vacuous.

source.place: Greco Theorem 5.3(i), reduction to local rings; Stacks Tag 00HT (lemma-flat-localization) and Tag 07GH (definition-G-ring).

proof.text: The localized map $g$ is weakly etale, as follows directly from the flat multiplication criterion. Put $T=B\otimes_A B$ and $U=B\setminus\mathfrak q$. The $T$-module $B$, via multiplication, is flat; [lem-pc-affine-flat-module-localization-preserves-flatness] with this $B$-module and $U$ shows that $S=U^{-1}B$ is flat over $T$. The ring $S\otimes_R S$ is the localization of $T$ obtained by inverting $b\otimes1$ and $1\otimes b$ for $b\in U$: the forward map sends $(b/u)\otimes(c/w)$ to $(b\otimes c)/((u\otimes1)(1\otimes w))$, and the inverse sends $b\otimes c$ to $(b/1)\otimes(c/1)$ and inverts the displayed denominator factors. The balancing relations hold over $A$, and elements of $A\setminus\mathfrak p$ are already units in both factors. Its action on $S$ is multiplication. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-over-localization], $S$ is flat over $S\otimes_R S$. Together with step 1 this is the two-flatness definition [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra].

source.place: Tag 00HT (lemma-flat-localization), parts (2) and (6); weak etaleness criterion, Tag 092B (definition-weakly-etale).

proof.text: For each prime $\mathfrak t\subset R$ put $k_{\mathfrak t}=\kappa(\mathfrak t)$ and $F_{\mathfrak t}=S\otimes_R k_{\mathfrak t}$. This fibre is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-noetherian] and weakly etale over the field $k_{\mathfrak t}$ by the base-change clause of [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability]. The ind-etale conclusion of [lem-weil-pbc-weak-etale-field] gives a filtered presentation by etale algebras over this field. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-henselization-finite-separable-fibres] to $k_{\mathfrak t}\to F_{\mathfrak t}$ at the zero prime of the base field. It gives a finite product $F_{\mathfrak t}\cong\prod_{i=1}^r L_i$ with every $L_i/k_{\mathfrak t}$ separable algebraic. The factors are the residue fields $\kappa(\mathfrak s_i)$ of the primes of $S$ contracting to $\mathfrak t$: prime ideals and residue fields on both sides agree by taking first the quotient by $\mathfrak t$ and then inverting the elements of $R\setminus\mathfrak t$. The empty product is allowed if the fibre is empty.

At $\mathfrak t=\mathfrak m_R$ the closed fibre $S/\mathfrak m_RS$ is nonzero and local, since $\mathfrak m_RS\subseteq\mathfrak m_S$ and it is a quotient of $S$. A nonzero finite product of fields is local only when there is one factor: for two nonzero coordinate idempotents $e$ and $1-e$, neither is a unit, contradicting locality. Thus this fibre is $L=\kappa(\mathfrak m_S)$ and $L/k_{\mathfrak m_R}$ is separable algebraic by step 3. By [lem-exc-separable-algebraic-square-zero-lifting], every $k_{\mathfrak m_R}$-algebra map from $L$ to a square-zero quotient lifts. The maximal ideal of $L$ is zero, so every such map kills its first power. This is exactly formal smoothness of the closed fibre for its maximal-ideal-adic topology by [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic].

source.place: Tag 0322 (proposition-characterize-separable-field-extensions), square-zero lifting; Greco Theorem 5.3(i), the separable algebraic closed fibre in Remark 5.2.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-formally-smooth-closed-fibre-adic] to the flat local map $g:R\to S$ of step 1 and the formally smooth closed fibre of step 4. It gives formal smoothness of $S/R$ for the $\mathfrak m_S$-adic topology. Now [lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-complete-source-target] gives the coordinate homomorphism $\widehat g:\widehat R\to\widehat S$ and formal smoothness of $\widehat S/\widehat R$ for the $\mathfrak m_S\widehat S$-adic topology. The map sends a compatible sequence represented by $r_n\bmod\mathfrak m_R^n$ to $g(r_n)\bmod\mathfrak m_S^n$; locality of $g$ makes these maps well-defined and compatible. Both $\widehat g\circ u$ and $v\circ g$ send $r$ to $g(r)\bmod\mathfrak m_S^n$ at every level, hence they agree.

source.place: Tag 07NQ (proposition-fs-flat-fibre-fs), (2) implies (3); Tag 07ED (lemma-formally-smooth-completion), (1) implies (3); Greco Theorem 5.3(i), completed-local-map argument.

proof.text: For $T=R,S$, the completion $\widehat T$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian]. Its maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_T$ is finitely generated since $T$ is Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal], $\widehat T$ is complete for $I_T=\mathfrak m_T\widehat T$ and $\widehat T/I_T\cong T/\mathfrak m_T$, a field. By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-complete-jacobson-radical], every maximal ideal contains $I_T$; the field quotient then forces $I_T$ to be the unique maximal ideal. The first-coordinate formula in step 5 sends the kernel of $\widehat R\to R/\mathfrak m_R$ into that of $\widehat S\to S/\mathfrak m_S$, so $\widehat g$ is local. Thus step 5 supplies exactly the formal-smoothness hypothesis for this local map of complete Noetherian local rings, and [lem-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-complete-local-regular] proves $\widehat g$ regular.

source.place: Tag 07PM (proposition-fs-regular), (4) implies (1); completion properties: Algebra Tag 0316 (lemma-completion-Noetherian-Noetherian), Tag 05GG (lemma-hathat-finitely-generated), Tag 05GI (lemma-radical-completion).

proof.text: The ring $\widehat S$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian]. For every prime $\mathfrak t\subset R$, its fibre $\widehat S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak t)$ is therefore Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-noetherian]. The regular maps $u$ from step 1 and $\widehat g$ from step 6 consequently satisfy every hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-regular-composition]. Their composite $h=v\circ g:R\to\widehat S$ is regular. In particular $D_{\mathfrak t}=\widehat S\otimes_R k_{\mathfrak t}$ is geometrically regular over $k_{\mathfrak t}$.

source.place: Tags 0316 (lemma-completion-Noetherian-Noetherian) and 07QI (lemma-regular-composition); Greco Theorem 5.3(i), composite-map sentence.

proof.text: Fix $\mathfrak t$ and the finite product $F_{\mathfrak t}=\prod_iL_i$ of step 3. By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-cancel-base-change], $D_{\mathfrak t}\cong\widehat S\otimes_SF_{\mathfrak t}$. The maps $c\otimes(x_i)_i\mapsto(c\otimes x_i)_i$ and $(c_i\otimes x_i)_i\mapsto\sum_i c_i\otimes e_ix_i$, extended additively, are mutually inverse: $e_ix_i$ denotes $x_i$ inserted in the $i$th coordinate and zero elsewhere; the $e_i$ are the finitely many orthogonal coordinate idempotents and sum to one. They give $D_{\mathfrak t}\cong\prod_i C_i$, where $C_i=\widehat S\otimes_S L_i=\widehat S\otimes_S\kappa(\mathfrak s_i)$, compatibly with the $k_{\mathfrak t}$-actions. Each $C_i$ is the localization of $D_{\mathfrak t}$ at $e_i$; explicitly all other coordinate idempotents become zero and the $i$th becomes one.

source.place: Greco Theorem 5.3(i), final formal-fibre argument, expanded as in Stacks Tag 0AH3 (lemma-henselization-pair-G-ring), displayed finite-product identity.

proof.text: Each $C_i$ is geometrically regular over $k_{\mathfrak t}$. Indeed it is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-noetherian], applied to $S\to\widehat S$ at $\mathfrak s_i$. For any finite purely inseparable field extension $K/k_{\mathfrak t}$, $K\otimes_{k_{\mathfrak t}}C_i$ is the localization of $K\otimes_{k_{\mathfrak t}}D_{\mathfrak t}$ at $1\otimes e_i$, via $(a\otimes d)/(1\otimes e_i)^n\mapsto a\otimes(d/e_i^n)$, with inverse $a\otimes(d/e_i^n)\mapsto(a\otimes d)/(1\otimes e_i)^n$. The balancing and localization relations make these maps well-defined and their composites fix every displayed generator. The latter ring is regular by step 7 and [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]; [lem-weil-pbc-localization-of-regular-ring] makes its localization regular. This is exactly the definition of geometric regularity of $C_i$.

source.place: Tag 0381 (lemma-geometrically-regular), localization argument in its proof; Tag 0AH3, extraction of a formal-fibre component.

proof.text: For every prime $\mathfrak s\subset S$, choose its contraction $\mathfrak t$ and its factor $L_i=\kappa(\mathfrak s)$ in step 3. Step 9 gives $\widehat S\otimes_S\kappa(\mathfrak s)$ geometrically regular over $k_{\mathfrak t}$. The extension $\kappa(\mathfrak s)/k_{\mathfrak t}$ is separable algebraic, and this fibre is Noetherian as already checked, so [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-regularity-separable-extension] gives geometric regularity over $\kappa(\mathfrak s)$ itself. The map $v$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-faithfully-flat]. By [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] it is therefore regular. Since the original prime $\mathfrak q\subset B$ was arbitrary and $B$ is Noetherian by hypothesis, the same definition gives that $B$ is a G-ring.
